guideTitle: The Best Laptop Docking Stations, From $27 Hubs to Thunderbolt 4
metaTitle: Best Docking Stations for Laptops: USB-C Hubs and Thunderbolt 4 Docks (2026)
metaDescription: We compared laptop docking stations on display outputs, charging, ports and Thunderbolt certification, from budget UGREEN and Anker hubs to Plugable and UGREEN Thunderbolt 4 docks.
introParagraphs: A laptop dock turns one cable into a desk setup: monitors, keyboard, mouse, network and charging. The first decision is between a USB-C hub, which is inexpensive and passes through your laptop charger's power, and a powered dock or Thunderbolt 4 dock, which costs more and adds its own power and bandwidth.

Then check what your laptop supports. Two or three external monitors through a dock depend on the laptop's USB-C or Thunderbolt port; many laptops, and base Apple M-series MacBooks, support fewer external displays than a dock's port count suggests. Thunderbolt 4 certification helps with compatibility on Thunderbolt laptops.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $27 to $200 at the time of writing.

anker-prime-docking-station-14-port.summary: A 14-port dock with up to 160W output, 10Gbps data and dual 4K support.
anker-prime-docking-station-14-port.description:
The Anker Prime is the most complete non-Thunderbolt dock here: 14 ports, up to 160W total output, 10Gbps data and dual 4K display support, listed for Dell, HP, Lenovo and other Windows laptops.

It suits a permanent desk with many peripherals and a laptop that should charge through the dock.

It costs about $170 at the time of writing, close to the Thunderbolt docks.
anker-prime-docking-station-14-port.skipIf: You have a Thunderbolt laptop; a certified TB4 dock may suit better at a similar price.

anker-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.summary: An 8-in-1 hub with two HDMI ports, gigabit Ethernet, 85W pass-through and SD.
anker-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.description:
The Anker 8-in-1 is the budget pick if you need wired networking: two HDMI outputs listed for dual 4K, gigabit Ethernet, 85W power pass-through and an SD slot, for about $54 at the time of writing.

Dual displays depend on your laptop, and you need your own charger for pass-through.
anker-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.bestFor: Home offices that need Ethernet and two monitors.
anker-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.skipIf: You do not need Ethernet; the UGREEN 7-in-1 costs half as much.

ugreen-7-in-1-docking-station-revodok-pr.summary: An aluminum 7-in-1 hub with dual 4K 60Hz HDMI, 10Gbps data and 100W pass-through.
ugreen-7-in-1-docking-station-revodok-pr.description:
The UGREEN 7-in-1 is the lowest-priced option here at about $27 at the time of writing, with two HDMI outputs listed for 4K 60Hz, 10Gbps USB-A and USB-C data, and 100W pass-through in an aluminum body.

It has no Ethernet or card reader.
ugreen-7-in-1-docking-station-revodok-pr.bestFor: Simple two-monitor setups on a budget.
ugreen-7-in-1-docking-station-revodok-pr.skipIf: You need Ethernet; the Anker 8-in-1 has it.

anker-nano-13-in-1-laptop-docking-statio.summary: A 13-in-1 dock with two HDMI and a DisplayPort, plus a detachable 6-in-1 travel hub.
anker-nano-13-in-1-laptop-docking-statio.description:
The Anker Nano 13-in-1 supports three displays (two HDMI and one DisplayPort), with 10Gbps USB-C, three USB-A ports and up to 100W power delivery.

Its detachable 6-in-1 module can travel with you while the main dock stays on the desk.

Three displays depend on your laptop, and it costs about $120 at the time of writing.
specs: Displays: up to 3 (2 x HDMI, 1 x DP)
anker-nano-13-in-1-laptop-docking-statio.skipIf: You use one or two monitors; a cheaper hub is enough.

acer-usb-c-docking-station-9-in-1.summary: An Acer 9-in-1 hub with two HDMI ports for about $35.
acer-usb-c-docking-station-9-in-1.description:
The Acer 9-in-1 offers two HDMI ports for about $35 at the time of writing.

The listing gives few other details: no power delivery, data speed or Ethernet information. Check the full listing before buying.
acer-usb-c-docking-station-9-in-1.bestFor: Simple two-monitor setups, especially with an Acer laptop.
acer-usb-c-docking-station-9-in-1.skipIf: You want stated specifications; the UGREEN 7-in-1 lists more for less.

anker-nano-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.summary: A pocket-size 8-in-1 hub with 4K HDMI, 10Gbps USB-C, SD/TF and 85W pass-through.
anker-nano-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.description:
The Anker Nano 8-in-1 is the compact option: 4K 60Hz HDMI, a 10Gbps USB-C port, two USB-A ports, an SD/TF reader and 85W pass-through, for about $30 at the time of writing.

It suits travel as well as the desk.
anker-nano-laptop-docking-station-8-in-1.skipIf: You need Ethernet; the Anker 8-in-1 has it.

plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.summary: A certified, driverless Thunderbolt 4 dock with 100W charging, dual 4K or single 6K.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.description:
The Plugable TBT-UDM is Thunderbolt 4 certified, which means it has passed Intel's certification for compatibility with Thunderbolt laptops. It is driverless, charges at 100W, and supports dual 4K HDMI displays or a single 6K display, with six USB ports, SD and Ethernet.

It costs about $200 at the time of writing, the most here.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.bestFor: Thunderbolt laptops that should charge and connect through one cable.
plugable-thunderbolt-4-dock-tbt-udm.skipIf: Your laptop lacks Thunderbolt; a USB-C hub costs far less.

ugreen-8-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max-.summary: A certified Thunderbolt 4 dock with three TB4 ports, dual 4K or single 8K, and 85W charging.
ugreen-8-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max-.description:
The UGREEN Revodok Max 208 is a Thunderbolt 4 certified dock at 40Gbps with three Thunderbolt 4 ports, supporting dual 4K 60Hz or a single 8K display, 85W charging, gigabit Ethernet and three USB-A ports.

UGREEN lists compatibility with Macs from M1 to M4 Pro and Max. It costs about $25 less than the Plugable at the time of writing, with less charging power.
ugreen-8-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max-.bestFor: Thunderbolt laptops that need extra Thunderbolt ports.
ugreen-8-in-1-thunderbolt-4-revodok-max-.skipIf: Your laptop needs more than 85W; the Plugable offers 100W.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Hubs pass through your charger's power; powered and Thunderbolt docks supply their own.
Two or three outputs only help if the laptop can drive them. Check its documentation.
Match or exceed your laptop charger's wattage: 85W to 160W here.
Ethernet, SD readers and fast USB vary. Buy the ports you use.
Certified docks (Plugable, UGREEN Max) suit Thunderbolt laptops and offer more bandwidth.

faq.q: Do I need a Thunderbolt dock?
faq.a: Only if your laptop has Thunderbolt and you want its bandwidth, or the dock's certification. A USB-C hub covers most simple setups.

faq.q: Will a dock charge my laptop?
faq.a: Powered docks do. Hubs pass through power from your charger; check the listed wattage.

faq.q: Why won't my second monitor show a separate image?
faq.a: Your laptop may support fewer external displays over USB-C than the dock has outputs, or may mirror. Check its documentation.

bottomLine: For most laptops, a hub is enough: the UGREEN 7-in-1 for two monitors at the lowest price, the Anker 8-in-1 if you need Ethernet, the Anker Nano for travel, and the Nano 13-in-1 for three displays.
For a Thunderbolt laptop, the UGREEN Revodok Max 208 is the value certified dock and the Plugable adds 100W charging. The Anker Prime suits Windows desks with many peripherals.
